title: Hackathons & competitions
what: Weekend build events (online and in-person). Prizes exist, but the real haul is a finished project, new contacts, and a deadline that forces you to ship.
firstStep: Pick one starting soon, go alone, aim to finish anything by demo time — not to win.
honestNote: You don't need to win to gain. Losers who shipped a project still have a project.

title: AI setup services for small businesses
what: Local shops and small businesses keep hearing about AI and have no idea what to do. You (with Path 3 skills) can set up chatbots, automation flows, and document summaries for them.
firstStep: Do one for free for a business you know — screenshots become your portfolio — then charge the next one.
honestNote: This is a service, not a product: you trade time for money. Real, but not passive.

title: Content in your language
what: Most AI tutorials exist only in English. Explainers in your native language face near-zero competition and genuine demand.
firstStep: Take any HELPinhex guide, record yourself explaining it in your language, publish.
honestNote: Ad/affiliate money starts tiny. The creators who win in small languages are the ones still posting in month 6.

title: Open-source contributions
what: Fix docs, reproduce bugs, add examples to AI repos. Zero money directly — but it's the strongest job/internship signal a beginner can build, and AI-assisted contribution is easier than ever.
firstStep: Pick a repo from the Repo Radar, find issues labeled 'good first issue', read the code with an AI tutor.
timeToFirst: weeks to first merged PR (the real paycheck)
honestNote: Maintainers can smell AI-generated slop PRs. Use AI to understand, not to write blind.

title: A tiny tool that solves one niche problem
what: One specific group has one annoying problem; you build the small tool that fixes it (with AI doing half the coding). $5/mo × 100 users = $500/mo.
firstStep: Find a problem you've personally complained about 3+ times, then find the community that complains with you.
honestNote: The hardest option here. Most fail from building for nobody — the community comes first, code second.

title: Teach what you just learned
what: The person 3 steps behind you needs a guide who just learned it — you remember exactly what was confusing. School clubs, libraries, Discord communities, paid workshops.
firstStep: Offer one free 45-min 'AI for absolute beginners' session anywhere people gather. Charge for session two.
timeToFirst: days to weeks — the fastest path here
honestNote: Teaching is the fastest way to learn. Your beginner status is literally the qualification.
